what_happened: Corpus audit (grep for pgrep -f, pkill -f, ps aux|grep / ps -ef|grep across agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/** and scripts/*.sh) found zero live violations of the exact-pid rule in the suite battery: the only historical occurrence (test-gate-registry-resolution.sh case13) was already fixed in-task (task 411) using kill -0 on a captured pid, and every other textual hit is either a comment documenting the anti-pattern, a fixture command string fed to validate-bounded-waiter.sh's own test suite (testing a DIFFERENT, already-existing agent-waiter-layer lint that enforces this same discipline on dispatched agents' Bash commands via bounded-build-waiter.md), or a doc/script passage already recommending the correct pattern. This means the standard's new subsection documents a corpus that is already compliant, and strongly informs the mechanical-lint question: ~20 textual hits, 0 violations, most would need a per-file allowlist -- the exact high-exemption-ratio condition the dispatch warned against for a mechanical check.

Writing the plan file via a Bash heredoc was refused by the PreToolUse bounded-waiter hook (validate-bounded-waiter.sh): the plan's PROSE quotes the process-name-match anti-pattern it is documenting, and the hook's textual shape detection fired on the heredoc command text. Worked around by using the Write tool instead. This is direct, in-dispatch evidence for the research report's lint-declination finding: a purely textual detector for this pattern has a real false-positive surface on documentation that discusses the pattern. The implement phase must author the standard's new subsection with Write/Edit rather than a shell heredoc for the same reason, and that hazard is recorded as a risk row in the plan.

Live collision reproduction against the already-fixed test-gate-registry-resolution.sh case13 cleanly demonstrated the exact-pid rule's value: an injected sibling sleep 30 process (same command text as the fixture) stayed alive through and after the suite run; case13 correctly reported no leftover against its own captured pid, while a standalone name-match probe matched the injected pid plus two other unrelated sleep 30 processes already alive on the host from concurrent sibling work -- live, unplanned corroboration of the exact collision risk the standard documents.

index-entries.json was already dirty at session start from a concurrent sibling task's uncommitted edit (patterns/file-footprint-overlap.md line_count 283 to 330), unrelated to this task. Phase 2 needed to commit its own, different hunk in the same file (the shell-script-testing.md entry). To avoid sweeping the foreign hunk into this task's commit, the foreign line was temporarily reverted to its HEAD value, this task's hunk was committed alone, and the foreign line was restored to its working-tree value immediately afterward -- never committed, never discarded. Recorded for traceability; no action needed from the owning sibling task.
